questions.passage: Nautilids are marine mollusks that begin growing their shells before emerging from their eggs and continue to add shell segments throughout their lifetimes. The walls between their shells’ chambers are called septa, and the deeper the water in which a septum forms, the greater the concentration of the isotope oxygen-18 the septum will contain. Since temperature falls as depth increases, if the area of ocean a nautilid inhabits is known, this isotopic signature can reveal the temperature at which its septa formed. Paleontologist Amane Tajika and colleagues examined each of the septa in two nautilid shells and concluded that septum sample M20 formed at a temperature of 15.2°C whereas sample F04 formed at 22.5°C.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researchers’ conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At a depth of 355 meters in the nautilids’ habitat, the water is 15.2°C and the concentration of oxygen-18 is equal to that in sample M20.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The concentration of oxygen-18 in F04 is lower than that in M20.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The concentration of oxygen-18 in F04 is higher than that in M20.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At a depth of 90 meters in the nautilids’ habitat, the water is 22.5°C and the concentration of oxygen-18 is equal to that in sample F04.

explanation.short: F04 cannot be both warmer and richer in oxygen-18 than M20 under the stated depth relationship.
explanation.key_evidence: Greater depth means more oxygen-18 and lower temperature.
explanation.why_correct: The text says oxygen-18 concentration rises with depth while temperature falls, so a septum assigned the warmer 22.5°C formation temperature should have less oxygen-18 than one assigned 15.2°C.
explanation.detailed: C gives the reverse ordering: warmer F04 has more oxygen-18 than cooler M20. Under the passage’s stated isotope-depth-temperature links, that result undermines the researchers’ temperature assignments.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“At a depth of 355 meters in the nautilids’ habitat, the water is 15.2°C and the concentration of oxygen-18 is equal to that in sample M20.”) is incorrect because it aligns M20’s isotope concentration with habitat water at the claimed 15.2°C, supporting rather than weakening its estimate.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“The concentration of oxygen-18 in F04 is lower than that in M20.”) is incorrect because it gives F04 less oxygen-18 than M20, the expected ordering for a warmer, shallower-forming septum.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“The concentration of oxygen-18 in F04 is higher than that in M20.”) is correct because it makes the warmer F04 sample richer in the isotope associated with colder, deeper water, contradicting the basis of the conclusion.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“At a depth of 90 meters in the nautilids’ habitat, the water is 22.5°C and the concentration of oxygen-18 is equal to that in sample F04.”) is incorrect because it matches F04’s isotope signature to water at the claimed 22.5°C, directly corroborating that estimate.

questions.passage: Interested in how differences in the color of dogs’ irises affect human responses to dogs, Akitsugu Konno et al. showed close-up images of dogs’ faces to human participants and asked them to rate the dogs’ traits and their own attitudes toward the dogs. Konno et al. suggest that differences in iris color led participants to view some dogs as more vulnerable and in need of protection than others and that this phenomenon could help explain the association the researchers observed between iris color and participants’ inclinations to interact with or keep dogs, as illustrated by the finding that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: participants rated the dog in image 3 as less mature than the dog in image 8 and rated the dog in image 14 as less mature than the dog in image 24.

choices.label: B
choices.text: dogs that participants rated as friendlier were also dogs that participants indicated a stronger willingness to interact with or keep.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the more mature a dog was perceived to be, the more likely participants were to rate it as having light irises.

choices.label: D
choices.text: participants favored the dogs in images 3 and 8, which they rated as less mature than the dogs in images 24 and 14.

explanation.short: The less-mature-looking dogs also receive the stronger keep/interact preferences.
explanation.key_evidence: Images3/8 have maturity2.51/2.91 and keep2.35/1.90; images14/24 have maturity3.27/4.03 and keep1.55/1.40. Interaction scores follow the same preference pattern.
explanation.why_correct: D connects perceived immaturity, a proposed cue to vulnerability, with the willingness to interact with or keep those dogs.
explanation.detailed: The hypothesis needs both a vulnerability-related perception and an approach/protection preference. The dark-iris dogs in images3/8 are judged less mature and favored more than the light-iris dogs in images14/24. A reports only maturity; B substitutes friendliness for the proposed vulnerability cue; C links maturity with iris color but leaves out preferences. D supplies the full relevant connection without proving causation by itself.

choice_analysis.A: The maturity comparisons are accurate but do not address willingness to keep or interact.
choice_analysis.B: Friendliness plus preference does not illustrate the proposed immaturity/vulnerability explanation.
choice_analysis.C: It omits keep/interact preferences; reversing an association's verbal direction alone would not invalidate it.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: it combines lower perceived maturity with higher preference for the same dogs.

questions.passage: Anthropogenic noise (sounds from human sources like traffic or mining) can affect animals, as Soledad Lucía Uran and colleagues found in a 2012 study of brown rats. A meta-analysis of more than 100 such studies examining various species found that, for every study, relevant traits or behaviors of the animals were observably different between the exposed group and the otherwise similar but unexposed group, regardless of whether that difference was beneficial or detrimental for the exposed group. So while a study of birds might show a difference that benefits the exposed group, and a study of mammals might show a difference that’s harmful to the exposed group, both differences are substantial. Therefore, the results of the meta-analysis suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: exposure to anthropogenic noise will likely have noticeable effects both on mammals such as brown rats and on birds such as reed buntings, but the nature of that effect could be very different for the two species.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the studies of the birds likely found significantly larger effects of exposure to anthropogenic noise than most studies of mammals except the study of brown rats by Soledad Lucía Uran and colleagues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the studies in the meta-analysis that examined mammals were more likely than those about birds to specify whether the observed effects were detrimental.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the study conducted by Soledad Lucía Uran and colleagues found substantial differences, but studies included in the meta-analysis of mammals other than brown rats likely did not.

explanation.short: Human-made noise likely affects both mammals and birds noticeably, though the effect can differ in direction.
explanation.key_evidence: Every study found an observable exposed-versus-unexposed difference, whether beneficial or harmful.
explanation.why_correct: The supplied text and evidence establish the connection: The meta-analysis found substantial effects across species without requiring those effects to have the same sign, so mammals and birds can both be affected even when one benefits and the other is harmed.
explanation.detailed: A preserves both conclusions supported by the evidence: broad detectability and variable nature. The analysis does not rank effect sizes by animal group or say most mammal studies lacked substantial results.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“exposure to anthropogenic noise will likely have noticeable effects both on mammals such as brown rats and on birds such as reed buntings, but the nature of that effect could be very different for the two species.”) is correct because it reflects the cross-species finding and allows the effect on brown rats to differ from the effect on reed buntings.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“the studies of the birds likely found significantly larger effects of exposure to anthropogenic noise than most studies of mammals except the study of brown rats by Soledad Lucía Uran and colleagues.”) is incorrect because it claims bird effects were larger than mammal effects, but the text discusses direction and observability, not a size ranking by class.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“the studies in the meta-analysis that examined mammals were more likely than those about birds to specify whether the observed effects were detrimental.”) is incorrect because it speculates about which studies specified harm; the passage states examples of beneficial and detrimental effects without that reporting comparison.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“the study conducted by Soledad Lucía Uran and colleagues found substantial differences, but studies included in the meta-analysis of mammals other than brown rats likely did not.”) is incorrect because it contradicts the statement that every study found an observable difference by suggesting other mammal studies likely did not.

questions.passage: To measure changes in parasite abundance over time, Chelsea Wood and colleagues counted parasite individuals preserved on specimens of striped sea perch, surf smelt, and six other fish species collected from Puget Sound between 1880 and 2019. Using statistical models to estimate historical populations, the researchers determined that for every 1°C increase in annual average sea surface temperature, the abundance of complex life cycle parasites like [i]Lecithaster sp.[/i] that require at least three unique host species throughout their life cycle decreased by 38%. However, the abundance of [i]Bomolochus bellones[/i] and other directly transmitted parasites, which require only one host species, was essentially unchanged. These findings suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: [i]Lecithaster sp.[/i] abundance decreased by 38% over the period studied, whereas [i]B. bellones[/i] abundance did not.

choices.label: B
choices.text: parasites that rely exclusively on either striped sea perch or surf smelt are more sensitive to rising temperatures than are parasites that can infect both species throughout their life cycles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: dependency on only a single host species may confer on parasites some resilience to rising sea surface temperatures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: as the number of hosts that complex life cycle parasites require increases, the parasites’ tolerance for rising sea surface temperatures decreases proportionally.

explanation.short: Requiring only one host may make directly transmitted parasites more resilient to warming seas.
explanation.key_evidence: Complex parasites fell 38% per 1°C; one-host parasites were essentially unchanged.
explanation.why_correct: The text contrasts temperature-linked decline in parasites needing at least three host species with stability in parasites needing one, supporting the inference that single-host dependence can confer resilience.
explanation.detailed: The conclusion should generalize cautiously from the observed difference in life-cycle complexity. C does so with “may,” whereas the data do not establish an exact decline over the entire period or a proportional rule for every added host.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“[i]Lecithaster sp.[/i] abundance decreased by 38% over the period studied, whereas [i]B. bellones[/i] abundance did not.”) is incorrect because it mistakes the rate: abundance fell 38% for each 1°C increase, not necessarily 38% across the full 1880–2019 period.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“parasites that rely exclusively on either striped sea perch or surf smelt are more sensitive to rising temperatures than are parasites that can infect both species throughout their life cycles.”) is incorrect because it invents sensitivity tied specifically to striped sea perch or surf smelt and to the ability to infect both; the study groups parasites by host-count requirement.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“dependency on only a single host species may confer on parasites some resilience to rising sea surface temperatures.”) is correct because it matches the stability of one-host parasites relative to the warming-related decline of complex life-cycle parasites.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“as the number of hosts that complex life cycle parasites require increases, the parasites’ tolerance for rising sea surface temperatures decreases proportionally.”) is incorrect because it claims a proportional decrease in tolerance with every additional host, a precise dose-response relationship the two-category comparison cannot establish.

questions.passage: The historian’s books about Millard Fillmore ______ what she is best known for, but she is also well regarded for her scholarship on Thomas Jefferson.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: is

choices.label: B
choices.text: are

choices.label: C
choices.text: has been

choices.label: D
choices.text: was

explanation.short: Are agrees with the plural subject books.
explanation.key_evidence: The core clause is 'The historian's books ... are what she is best known for.'
explanation.why_correct: Books is the grammatical subject, so the finite verb must be plural; are is the only plural option.
explanation.detailed: Remove the modifier 'about Millard Fillmore' to see the subject-verb pair clearly. The sentence describes the books' role in the historian's reputation. Is, has been, and was are all singular. Present perfect does not inherently mean a completed past condition; C fails here because has does not agree with books.

choice_analysis.A: Is is singular and disagrees with books.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: are is the plural present form required by books.
choice_analysis.C: Has been uses singular has; plural books would require have, regardless of whether a perfect tense were suitable.
choice_analysis.D: Was is singular; books cannot take that form.

questions.passage: Disyllabic words ______ as trochees in English metrical verse, such as “eyebrow” and “mascot,” consist of one stressed syllable followed by one unstressed syllable.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: have been classified

choices.label: B
choices.text: can be classified

choices.label: C
choices.text: are classified

choices.label: D
choices.text: classified

explanation.short: “Classified as trochees” is a reduced modifier describing “Disyllabic words.”
explanation.key_evidence: Main predicate: the words “consist of one stressed syllable followed by one unstressed syllable.”
explanation.why_correct: The sentence already has the finite verb “consist,” so the blank should contain the past participle “classified” to form a reduced relative clause modifying the words.
explanation.detailed: Expanding the modifier gives “Disyllabic words that are classified as trochees ... consist ...”. Adding another finite or modal verb in the blank would create two competing predicates with no connector.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“have been classified”) is incorrect because it is a finite verb phrase and clashes with the later finite verb “consist.”
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“can be classified”) is incorrect because it likewise creates an unjoined second predicate before “consist.”
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“are classified”) is incorrect because it produces two finite verbs, “are classified” and “consist,” without a relative pronoun or conjunction.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“classified”) is correct because it functions nonfinitely as a modifier, leaving “consist” as the sentence’s sole main verb.

questions.passage: All member nations of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, or NATO— including Belgium, which joined in 1949; Hungary, which joined in 1999; and Slovenia, which joined in ______ are committed to NATO’s principle of collective defense, each member pledging to defend all others.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.short: The closing em dash completes the interruption that begins after “NATO.”
explanation.key_evidence: Dash pair: “NATO—including Belgium ... Hungary ... and Slovenia ...—are committed.”
explanation.why_correct: The list of example nations interrupts the main clause, so the punctuation after Slovenia’s joining year must close the opening em dash before the sentence returns to “are committed.”
explanation.detailed: Semicolons inside the list separate the three members and their dates; they do not close the outer parenthetical construction. A matching em dash restores the main sentence “All member nations ... are committed.”

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“2004;”) is incorrect because its semicolon would continue or terminate an internal list division but would leave the opening em dash unmatched.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“2004”) is incorrect because it supplies no mark to close the dash-delimited interruption before the main verb.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“2004—”) is correct because it provides the matching em dash that brackets the entire “including ...” example list.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“2004,”) is incorrect because it uses a comma to close an interruption opened by an em dash, creating mismatched boundary punctuation.

questions.passage:
校订说明：编辑校订：依据 NASA 光谱资料，将源文颠倒的波长关系改为“蓝移波长较短、红移波长较长”；未改动语法题干和选项。

As the exoplanet 81 Ceti b orbits a star 330 light-years from Earth, the exoplanet’s gravity causes the star to wobble. In 2008, astronomers ______ this wobble through shifts in the color of the star’s spectral light—blueshifts indicating shorter wavelengths and movement toward the observer, redshifts longer wavelengths and movement away—deduced that the fluctuation was caused by the gravitational force of a previously undetected exoplanet.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: perceived

choices.label: B
choices.text: had perceived

choices.label: C
choices.text: were perceiving

choices.label: D
choices.text: perceiving

explanation.short: “Perceiving” modifies astronomers; “deduced” supplies the sentence's main verb.
explanation.key_evidence: The core clause is “astronomers ... deduced that the fluctuation was caused by ... an exoplanet.”
explanation.why_correct: D forms the participial phrase perceiving this wobble, identifying the astronomers who made the deduction. It does not introduce a second finite predicate competing with deduced.
explanation.detailed: Temporarily set aside the long wavelength explanation between dashes. The sentence reads In 2008, astronomers perceiving this wobble through shifts in the color of the star's spectral light deduced that .... The noun astronomers has the finite past-tense verb deduced. A present participle can modify that noun even when the main action is in the past; perceiving is not itself a present-tense main verb. The three finite-verb alternatives would need an additional conjunction or clause structure that the sentence does not supply.

choice_analysis.A: Perceived is a finite past-tense verb here, leaving astronomers perceived ... deduced with two uncoordinated predicates.
choice_analysis.B: Had perceived introduces a finite past-perfect predicate but provides no conjunction linking it to deduced.
choice_analysis.C: Were perceiving introduces a finite past-progressive predicate; deduced would then remain an unlinked second predicate.
choice_analysis.D: Perceiving is a nonfinite participle modifying astronomers, leaving deduced as the complete clause's main verb.

questions.passage: A loose confederation of cities from eleven modern-day countries, the Hanseatic League was a powerful mercantile alliance that dominated northern European trade between the 13th and 17th centuries. Hanseatic League member ______ was serendipitously located on the Rhine River in Germany, giving Cologne’s merchants access to key maritime trade routes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: city Cologne,

choices.label: B
choices.text: city, Cologne,

choices.label: C
choices.text: city, Cologne

choices.label: D
choices.text: city Cologne

explanation.short: “Cologne” directly identifies which Hanseatic League member city is meant, so no commas are needed.
explanation.key_evidence: Essential noun phrase: “Hanseatic League member city Cologne.”
explanation.why_correct: Because “city” does not independently identify a unique referent, the proper noun “Cologne” is essential to the subject and should be integrated without commas.
explanation.detailed: The completed subject is followed immediately by the main verb “was.” Treating Cologne as a removable aside would leave the vague phrase “Hanseatic League member city was ...,” which does not identify the city being discussed.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“city Cologne,”) is incorrect because it places a comma after the essential name, incorrectly separating the subject from its verb.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“city, Cologne,”) is incorrect because it surrounds “Cologne” with commas as if it were nonessential, although “member city” alone does not identify the subject.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“city, Cologne”) is incorrect because it opens a comma interruption before “Cologne” but never closes it before “was.”
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“city Cologne”) is correct because it keeps the identifying name unpunctuated within the complete subject “member city Cologne.”

questions.passage: The moon Dia orbits Jupiter in the same direction that the planet rotates. ______ Dia’s orbit is described as prograde. Erinome, another of Jupiter’s moons, orbits in the opposite direction, so its orbit is described with the opposite term: retrograde.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: However,

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thus,

choices.label: C
choices.text: Likewise,

choices.label: D
choices.text: Next,

explanation.short: Dia moves in the planet’s rotation direction; thus, its orbit is classified as prograde.
explanation.key_evidence: Same direction as Jupiter’s rotation → prograde orbit.
explanation.why_correct: The second sentence states the classification that follows from the orbital direction given in the first, so “Thus” correctly marks a result.
explanation.detailed: The following Erinome example then supplies the opposite case, retrograde. The blank itself does not introduce that contrast; it connects Dia’s observed motion to the technical term for it.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“However,”) is incorrect because it would signal contradiction, but “prograde” is consistent with orbiting in the same direction as rotation.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“Thus,”) is correct because it accurately introduces the consequence or label derived from Dia’s direction.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“Likewise,”) is incorrect because it would require a prior parallel classification, which the first sentence does not provide.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“Next,”) is incorrect because it signals mere sequence and fails to express the logical relation between direction and classification.

questions.passage: Scientists studying asteroid deflection have focused on secondary objects such as S/2015 (190208), a moonlet orbiting the near-Earth asteroid 2006 AQ. In 2022 NASA intentionally crashed a probe into just such an object, successfully altering its orbit. Scientists have yet to demonstrate, ______ that 2006 AQ and other primary objects would be similarly affected.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: for example,

choices.label: B
choices.text: admittedly,

choices.label: C
choices.text: moreover,

choices.label: D
choices.text: likewise,

explanation.short: “Admittedly” concedes a remaining limitation after the successful moonlet-deflection result.
explanation.key_evidence: NASA altered a secondary object, but effects on primary asteroids remain unproved.
explanation.why_correct: The final sentence acknowledges that the promising demonstration does not yet establish the same outcome for primary objects, so a concessive transition is required.
explanation.detailed: “Admittedly” lets the writer grant a qualification to the preceding success. The sentence is not another example or an additional supporting point; it narrows what the evidence proves.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“for example,”) is incorrect because it would present the lack of proof as an illustration of the successful deflection, rather than a limitation on it.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“admittedly,”) is correct because it appropriately signals the concession that primary-object effects remain undemonstrated.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“moreover,”) is incorrect because it treats the limitation as additive support and misses the shift from success to uncertainty.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“likewise,”) is incorrect because it suggests a parallel demonstrated result, even though the sentence says similar effects have not been shown.

questions.passage: Many paintings of the trompe l’oeil genre attain their illusory verisimilitude by depicting quotidian things, such as a fly or an empty bird cage, as if they are placed directly on top of the painted canvas. Nicola van Houbraken’s 1700 trompe l’oeil [i]Portrait of François Rivière[/i], ______ startles the viewer with the extraordinary sight of a man appearing to poke his head out from within the picture frame.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: fittingly,

choices.label: B
choices.text: by contrast,

choices.label: C
choices.text: for instance,

choices.label: D
choices.text: specifically,

explanation.short: Unlike ordinary-object illusions, Houbraken’s painting uses the extraordinary image of a head emerging from the frame.
explanation.key_evidence: Many works depict a fly or empty cage; this portrait shows a man apparently poking out.
explanation.why_correct: The second sentence replaces the genre’s usual quotidian subject matter with a startling extraordinary sight, so “by contrast” marks the difference.
explanation.detailed: Both sentences describe trompe l’oeil technique, but their depicted subjects occupy opposite ends of an ordinary-to-extraordinary contrast. The transition should foreground that opposition.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“fittingly,”) is incorrect because it would suggest the extraordinary head is expected from the ordinary-object pattern just described, which it is not.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“by contrast,”) is correct because it correctly opposes the common flies and cages with the startling emerging man.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“for instance,”) is incorrect because it would make the portrait an example of depicting a quotidian object, but its subject is explicitly extraordinary.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“specifically,”) is incorrect because it would narrow the first claim, although the portrait departs from rather than specifies the usual approach.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Katrin Heer, Larissa Albrecht, and Elisabeth K.V. Kalko published a study in 2010.
• In it, the researchers found that ingestion by bats had a neutral effect on the germination of [i]Ficus nymphaeifolia[/i] plant seeds.
• Mikaela Marques Pulzatto and M.S. Dainez Filho published a study in 2017.
• In it, the researchers found that ingestion by bats had a negative effect on the germination of [i]Ficus luschnathiana[/i] plant seeds.
• Reinaldo Chaves Teixeira, C. Corrêa, and E. Fischer published a study in 2009.
• In it, the researchers found that ingestion by bats had a positive effect on the germination of [i]Ficus pertusa[/i] plant seeds.
questions.prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about the germination of seeds ingested by bats. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bat ingestion has consistently been found to have a positive effect on seed germination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As was found in the 2010 study, ingestion by bats has a positive effect on the germination of plant seeds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Over the years, researchers have studied the effect that seed germination has had on ingestion by bats.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Seed ingestion by bats can have varying effects on seed germination.

explanation.short: Bat ingestion can affect seed germination positively, negatively, or not at all.
explanation.key_evidence: The three studies report neutral, negative, and positive effects for three [i]Ficus[/i] species.
explanation.why_correct: The supplied text and evidence establish the connection: A valid generalization must accommodate all three study outcomes, and D does so by stating that the effect varies rather than assigning one consistent direction.
explanation.detailed: The notes span different years and plant species but do not support a single universal effect. “Varying effects” accurately summarizes the positive, negative, and neutral findings.

choice_analysis.A: Choice A (“Bat ingestion has consistently been found to have a positive effect on seed germination.”) is incorrect because it says the effect is consistently positive, contradicting the neutral 2010 and negative 2017 findings.
choice_analysis.B: Choice B (“As was found in the 2010 study, ingestion by bats has a positive effect on the germination of plant seeds.”) is incorrect because it misreports the 2010 result as positive when Heer and colleagues found a neutral effect.
choice_analysis.C: Choice C (“Over the years, researchers have studied the effect that seed germination has had on ingestion by bats.”) is incorrect because it reverses the causal question in the notes, which study how bat ingestion affects germination, not how germination affects ingestion.
choice_analysis.D: Choice D (“Seed ingestion by bats can have varying effects on seed germination.”) is correct because it is the only statement broad enough to include the observed neutral, negative, and positive outcomes.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• [i]Waiting[/i] is a 1987 black-and-white linocut print by Kuwaiti artist Thuraya Al-Baqsami.
• It depicts a tranquil, everyday scene (a woman in a headscarf gazing out a window).
• [i]¡Sera toda nuestra![/i] (“It will all be ours!”) is a 1977 color linocut print by Mexican American artist Carlos Cortéz.
• It features a scene with an explicitly political point of view (a group of laborers preparing to go on strike).
• Lino cutting is an inexpensive printmaking technique in which an image is carved onto linoleum tile, covered in ink or paint, and stamped onto paper.
questions.prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about linocut prints. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Linocuts can depict a range of scenes, from the explicitly political to the tranquil and everyday.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cortéz’s linocut features a group of laborers preparing to go on strike, while Al-Baqsami’s depicts a woman in a headscarf gazing out a window.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortéz made [i]¡Sera toda nuestra![/i] (“It will all be ours!”) in 1977, while Al-Baqsami made [i]Waiting[/i] later, in 1987.

choices.label: D

explanation.short: Linocut prints can portray both explicitly political action and tranquil everyday life.
explanation.key_evidence: Cortéz depicts striking laborers; Al-Baqsami depicts a woman quietly looking from a window.
explanation.why_correct: The supplied text and evidence establish the connection: The two examples support a general statement about the medium’s range, and A abstracts from them without merely retelling every detail.
explanation.detailed: One print is politically charged and the other domestic and calm, so together they demonstrate that linocut subject matter is not limited to a single tone or purpose.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, the city of Timbuktu was part of the Songhai Empire.
• Timbuktu was a center of trade and scholarship in the Sahara desert.
• The city was known for its hundreds of thousands of written manuscripts on both secular and religious subjects.
• The manuscripts survive today in dozens of private libraries across the city.
• [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i] is one of these manuscripts.
questions.prompt: The student wants to introduce [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i] to an audience unfamiliar with the Timbuktu manuscripts’ history. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, the city of Timbuktu was home to [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i], a manuscript that discusses trade centers across the Sahara desert.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the city of Timbuktu, dozens of private libraries house manuscripts, such as [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i], that discuss both secular and religious subjects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i] is a manuscript housed in a private library in Timbuktu.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Among Timbuktu’s vast collection of secular and religious manuscripts dating back to the Songhai Empire is [i]The Pearls Leading to Accepted Guidance[/i].

explanation.short: D introduces the named manuscript within Timbuktu's large Songhai-era manuscript tradition.
explanation.key_evidence: The notes connect Timbuktu's manuscript culture to the Songhai period and name this work as one surviving manuscript.
explanation.why_correct: An audience unfamiliar with that history benefits from the historical period, collection scale, and connection to the named manuscript, all supplied by D.
explanation.detailed: The goal is an introduction with historical context, not just current storage information. D frames the title as part of the extensive secular and religious collection associated with Songhai-era Timbuktu. B gives useful modern library context but omits that historical frame; C is still barer. A invents the work's specific subject.

choice_analysis.A: The notes call Timbuktu a trade center, not this manuscript a discussion of trade centers.
choice_analysis.B: It describes present libraries and broad subject coverage but does not supply the Songhai-era history that D provides.
choice_analysis.C: It gives only storage location and little context for an unfamiliar audience.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: it identifies the manuscript while supplying the broader historical collection context.
